title: Grand Principality of Moscow
capsule: The Grand Principality of Moscow emerged as a minor appanage of the Vladimir-Suzdal principality in 1263 under Daniel Alexandrovich, son of Alexander Nevsky, and by the 14th century had expanded through purchase, marriage, and inheritance to become the dominant Russian principality. Ivan III (r. 1462–1505) tripled its territory by annexing Novgorod (1478), Tver (1485), and Vyatka (1489), ended Tatar tribute payments after the Great Stand on the Ugra River (1480), and began styling himself ruler of all Rus. His grandson Ivan IV was crowned tsar in 1547, transforming the Grand Principality into the Tsardom of Russia and closing the period reflected in this dataset entry.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Moscow's territorial growth is well documented in Russian chronicle sources and treaty records from the 15th century onward; earlier 13th–14th century extents are approximated from principality boundary descriptions in chronicles and are less precise.
